anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L1 anchor is a static projected 5x5x3 extraction with four visible targets and low hazard/support counts. Rising Causeway d1 already adds first-person view control, staged support construction, a directional stair choice, physical launcher contact, and a post-launch terminal route.

evidence.explanation: Approved baseline table places the anchor at L1.
Its L1 profile is small and static, with one screen, one lava hazard, one support, and no sealed targets.
The anchor renders a projected voxel pile with rotate/mine/exit interactions.
Rising Causeway creates directional stair geometry and floor or wall launchers.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L3 anchor requires closed-loop tilt control through three ordered lamps while momentum, walls, wells, and bounce physics continue to evolve. Rising Causeway d4 has more explicit 3D route and actuator matching, but its walking and launch actions can be planned from visible geometry and no correct action expires during inference.

evidence.explanation: Approved baseline table places the anchor at L3.
The L3 anchor has three lamps, walls and hazards, and active board physics.
The anchor advances physics on fixed ticks and uses continuous full-mode drag control.
Its grader replays movement physics and ordered lamp/cup success.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L4 anchor has five face gates in an 18x11 route and hides die orientation between sparse scanners; every move changes the orientation needed by later gates. Rising Causeway d4 has substantial 3D motor and spatial demands, but its geometry, launcher normals, and terminal are visible and it has no comparable hidden-state memory or changing per-step route.

evidence.explanation: Approved baseline table places the anchor at L4.
Its L4 profile specifies five barriers, sparse orientation scanners, and a bounded roll range.
Movement changes orientation and gates movement on the current die face.
Its grader replays orientation and requires the ordered gate route.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L5 anchor requires four adjacent swaps on a changing 5x5 board, with multi-wave resolution and exact score/receipt constraints. Rising Causeway d4 has a short staged configuration sequence and one physical launch, not a comparable combinatorial chain where each accepted action changes the later decision board.

evidence.explanation: Approved baseline table places the anchor at L5.
Its L5 profile specifies four swaps and at least seven cascade waves.
Each accepted swap changes the visible board through collapse and refill.
Its grader replays the changing board and exact move/score constraints.

visible_baseline_solution.summary: A screenshot-only agent must read the first-person 3D chamber and console, click the red actuator until the HUD reaches three stages, choose the stair end that makes the far ledge high, select the blue launcher whose normal and landing geometry lead to the terminal, and use viewport drag plus held WASD/arrows to traverse the changed supports. It must approach the selected launcher without falling or crossing the wrong stair, allow the 840 ms contact launch to settle, walk to the far terminal, and click it within the 0.62 radius. The visible task supplies geometry, launcher IDs/normals, HUD state, position, and failure feedback; it does not supply private truth fields as instructions.
visible_baseline_solution.dependent_state: The red stage changes support, the selected stair controls walkable height, the primed launcher only launches on physical contact, and terminal activation requires exact staged configuration plus a completed landing.
visible_baseline_solution.precision_and_recovery: Full mode requires camera aim, block clicks, held movement, contact alignment, and final-radius positioning. Wrong stair, gap, outer-ledge, or invalid terminal actions fail the route.
visible_baseline_solution.timing_observation: The launch and settling sequence must be observed, but the source says no correct action expires solely while inference is pending; timing is not an independent real-time decision requirement.

evidence.explanation: The canvas renders the stair, decoys, launcher normals, terminal, and flight arc.
Movement, support checks, route failures, contact launch, gravity, and landing are implemented.
Full-mode input sources and actuator/terminal actions are bound to visible controls.
The independent replay rejects wrong sources, route failures, bad launch timing, wrong configuration, and terminal positions outside tolerance.

baseline_judgment.rationale: The current d4/full setting is plausibly a hard 3D control-and-planning task: it combines staged support construction, a directional height choice, a three-way launcher match, first-person movement, contact physics, and a narrow terminal tolerance. It is materially above the static L1 voxel anchor and adds a different spatial-control burden than the L3 gyroscopic anchor, while remaining below the changing-board dependency of the L5 candy anchor. Its position relative to the approved L4 Blind Dice Courier is mixed because Rising Causeway has stronger first-person motor demands but lacks hidden orientation memory. Keep d4 provisionally, but revise or calibrate the ladder because d4 to d5 adds no new staged dependency and the stair-side cue is not established as uniquely readable from the source.

evidence.explanation: The assigned baseline is difficulty 4/full and defines the three-stage, three-launcher reference chamber.
The generated world contains a mirror-dependent stair answer and a seeded launcher choice.
The route requires support-aware movement and a physical timed launch.
Success requires exact red/stair/launcher state, physical landing, and terminal reach.

uncertainties: No human or computer-use-agent calibration was available.
The source does not establish whether the pre-selection 3D view lets a screenshot-only agent infer the correct stair end reliably.
The absolute L3-versus-L4 placement is uncertain because the closest approved L4 anchor emphasizes hidden state while this task emphasizes first-person motor control.

profiles.visible_problem: Use labelled proxy controls to extend one red stage, choose one stair end, prime the only blue launcher, traverse a broad compact chamber, ride the contact launch, and activate the terminal.
profiles.success_condition: Reach red stage 1, the generated stair end, the only launcher, a valid landing, and the terminal within radius 0.8.
profiles.rationale: This is the family floor but remains a moving 3D route with dependent construction and launch contact, so it is above the static L1 anchor; the absence of launcher choice makes it a provisional L2.

evidence.explanation: D1 is compact, broad, and has one launcher with no decoys.
Simplified mode exposes proxy buttons while retaining the chamber and movement task.

profiles.visible_problem: Use viewport drag and canvas clicks for the same single-stage chamber, then held WASD/arrows for traversal, launch, landing, and terminal activation.
profiles.success_condition: Reach red stage 1, the generated stair end, the only launcher, a valid landing, and the terminal within radius 0.8.
profiles.rationale: The world and dependent route are the same as d1/simplified; direct camera and keyboard control add motor precision but not a new planning dependency.

evidence.explanation: The d1 world parameters are interaction-independent.
Full mode binds movement, look, and viewport actions to the same mechanics.

profiles.visible_problem: Use proxy controls for two red extensions, the stair, the single side-facing wall launcher, the longer narrower route, and the terminal.
profiles.success_condition: Reach red stage 2, the generated stair end and wall launcher, complete its landing, and activate the terminal within radius 0.75.
profiles.rationale: A second required support stage and lateral wall landing are active, but there is still only one actionable launcher; the decoy is visual clutter.

evidence.explanation: D2 adds a second stage, a wall launcher, and one decoy.
Difficulty 2 forces the required launcher to wall orientation and changes its landing.

profiles.visible_problem: Use direct camera and keyboard controls for the same two-stage, single-wall-launcher chamber with one noninteractive decoy.
profiles.success_condition: Reach red stage 2, the generated stair end and wall launcher, complete its landing, and activate the terminal within radius 0.75.
profiles.rationale: Direct input increases aiming and movement precision but leaves d2 information, support dependency, launcher count, and success state unchanged.

evidence.explanation: The d2 world parameters are independent of interaction mode.
Full mode uses direct keyboard, drag, and viewport click input.

profiles.visible_problem: Use proxy controls for two red stages and the stair, select one of two launcher entries by visible normal and landing geometry, traverse the narrower route, and activate the terminal after landing.
profiles.success_condition: Reach red stage 2, the required stair end and one of two required launchers, complete its landing, and activate the terminal within radius 0.7.
profiles.rationale: This is the first profile with a real launcher-selection decision and two possible landing geometries, plus tighter traversal and terminal precision; decoys add no actions.

evidence.explanation: D3 introduces two launchers and a narrower chamber.
The visible launcher gallery shows IDs, orientation lines, and selection state.

profiles.visible_problem: Use direct 3D camera clicks and held movement to choose the correct one of two visible launcher normals and landings, then complete the same two-stage route and terminal activation.
profiles.success_condition: Reach red stage 2, the required stair end and one of two required launchers, complete its landing, and activate the terminal within radius 0.7.
profiles.rationale: Full input adds spatial aiming and route-control precision to the first launcher-choice profile without changing the world or dependent success condition.

evidence.explanation: The d3 parameters are the same for full and simplified conditions.
Full mode uses direct viewport and keyboard sources with the same physics.

profiles.visible_problem: Use labelled proxies to reach three red stages, choose the stair high end, match one of three launchers to the terminal, traverse the narrow causeway, ride the contact launch, and activate the terminal.
profiles.success_condition: Reach red stage 3, the generated stair end and one of three required launchers, land physically, and activate the terminal within radius 0.62.
profiles.rationale: This hard profile has three dependent configuration choices, three launcher geometries, narrow clearance, contact physics, and tight terminal tolerance. Simplified controls reduce motor burden but preserve the world and effects.

evidence.explanation: D4 is the reference three-stage, three-launcher, narrow chamber.
The grader requires all configuration components, landing, and terminal reach.

profiles.visible_problem: Read the full first-person chamber, directly click the actuators, use held WASD/arrows through the narrow support, ride the selected launcher, and click the terminal.
profiles.success_condition: Reach red stage 3, the generated stair end and one of three required launchers, land physically, and activate the terminal within radius 0.62.
profiles.rationale: The current baseline combines the d4 planning burden with direct camera, click, held movement, and contact-positioning precision. It is a plausible L4 pending cue and calibration checks.

evidence.explanation: The declared baseline is d4/full.
Full interaction requires direct keyboard, drag, and viewport clicks.

profiles.visible_problem: Use proxies to reconcile four launcher entries with terminal height and offset while completing the three-stage extension, stair choice, narrow traversal, contact launch, and final activation.
profiles.success_condition: Reach red stage 3, the generated stair end and one of four required launchers, land physically, and activate the terminal within radius 0.55.
profiles.rationale: D5 is harder than d4 in choice count, clearance, launch geometry, and final precision, but red staging does not grow and no new state-changing dependency is introduced; it is a provisional high L4 rather than source-supported L5.

evidence.explanation: D5 adds a fourth launcher and tighter geometry but retains three red stages.
The extra launcher changes gallery and landing choices under the same mechanism.

profiles.visible_problem: Inspect the full 3D chamber, match one of four launcher normals and landing offsets to the terminal, then execute construction, narrow traversal, contact launch, landing, and final click.
profiles.success_condition: Reach red stage 3, the generated stair end and one of four required launchers, land physically, and activate the terminal within radius 0.55.
profiles.rationale: Direct motor precision makes d5 the hardest family profile, but its extra difficulty is mainly one choice and tighter geometry; without a new changing-state dependency or calibration it should not automatically be L5.

evidence.explanation: The d5/full world is defined by the d5 geometry with direct full input.
The same physical contact launch and route-failure rules apply in full mode.

adjacent_pairs.simplified_change: Red stages increase from one to two, length and stair rise increase, the corridor narrows, terminal tolerance tightens, and the sole required launcher changes to a wall-facing launcher; one noninteractive decoy is added.
adjacent_pairs.full_change: The same world and success changes apply with direct camera and keyboard input.
adjacent_pairs.ordering_assessment: A real additional support dependency and different launch geometry distinguish d2; decoy, route length, and lower speed are not independent planning complexity.

evidence.explanation: The active d1/d2 changes are explicit.
D2 forces wall orientation and a lateral landing.

adjacent_pairs.simplified_change: The launcher gallery grows from one to two, the route narrows and rises, terminal tolerance tightens, and a second decoy is added; red staging remains two.
adjacent_pairs.full_change: The same gallery and geometry changes apply under direct viewport and keyboard input.
adjacent_pairs.ordering_assessment: The new actionable launcher choice is genuine, but per-seed physical ordering is not uniform because d2 is always wall-facing while d3 can be floor-facing or wall-facing.

evidence.explanation: The d2-to-d3 changes include launcher count, width, stair height, and terminal radius.
Required launcher orientation varies in d3 but is fixed to wall in d2.

adjacent_pairs.simplified_change: Red stages increase from two to three, the gallery grows from two to three, the stair/chamber rise and length increase, the corridor narrows, terminal tolerance tightens, and another decoy is added.
adjacent_pairs.full_change: The same new construction stage, launcher choice, and tighter route apply with direct camera and keyboard input.
adjacent_pairs.ordering_assessment: This adds a required state transition and a further launcher match while reducing movement and terminal clearance.

evidence.explanation: The d3-to-d4 parameters show the extra red stage, launcher, and tighter geometry.
The additional stage is part of terminal success.

adjacent_pairs.simplified_change: The gallery grows from three to four, the chamber and stair extend, the corridor and terminal radius tighten, and movement speed drops; red stages remain three.
adjacent_pairs.full_change: The same fourth-choice and tighter-control changes apply under direct full input.
adjacent_pairs.ordering_assessment: The pair is structurally distinguishable but weakly separated: the extra launcher and tighter geometry matter, while decoys, longer traversal, and lower speed add no new state-changing decision. Calibration is needed before treating d5 as L5.

evidence.explanation: D4 and d5 retain red_stage_target 3 and change gallery/clearance parameters.
The added decoy is a question-mark block while launchers remain actionable.

baseline_preservation.current_default_equivalence: The generator defaults to difficulty 4 without a condition and the browser defaults to full interaction. World and rules therefore match explicit d4/full for the same seed, although condition-bearing challenge identity and metadata differ.
baseline_preservation.historical_preservation: Not established; the supplied source contains the current controlled implementation but no pre-controls implementation.

evidence.explanation: No condition defaults to difficulty 4 and explicit conditions override named profile parameters.
Condition presence changes the challenge token and exported condition.
The browser defaults to full interaction and derives route state from the public world.
Tests establish deterministic generation and full/simplified world equality for each level.

missing_evidence: Human or computer-use-agent success-rate and completion-time calibration across levels and seeds.

interaction_equivalence.input_surface_binding: Simplified emits proxy/control/look sources; full requires viewport clicks, keyboard movement, and viewport drag; the grader checks the selected interaction and source map.

evidence.explanation: Controlled full and simplified generation has equal worlds.
The grader binds source expectations to the interaction condition.

interaction_equivalence.world_and_information: Both modes receive the same two-stage chamber, single wall launcher, decoy, and projected geometry; simplified adds labelled proxies.
interaction_equivalence.goal_and_effects: Red stage, stair, wall-launch contact, landing, movement, and terminal effects are unchanged.
interaction_equivalence.physics_timing_tolerances_success: Shared wall-launch trajectory, fixed duration, route checks, and radius 0.75 terminal tolerance.
interaction_equivalence.input_surface_binding: Mode-specific sources are emitted and the grader rejects a transcript using the other mode's source map.

evidence.explanation: Input handlers select mode-specific sources while invoking the same actions.
The grader checks world equality, condition, and interaction sources.

interaction_equivalence.world_and_information: Both modes receive the same two-launcher gallery and d3 geometry; simplified names launcher entries while full renders positions and normals.
interaction_equivalence.goal_and_effects: The two-stage support route, stair choice, launcher choice, physical launch, landing, and terminal effects are unchanged.
interaction_equivalence.physics_timing_tolerances_success: Shared contact radius, launch trajectory, route checks, and radius 0.7 terminal tolerance.
interaction_equivalence.input_surface_binding: Proxy and direct sources are enforced in the browser payload and independent replay.

interaction_equivalence.world_and_information: Both modes receive the same three-stage, three-launcher d4 chamber and public geometry; simplified labels expose actions as proxies.
interaction_equivalence.goal_and_effects: The same red/stair/launcher configuration, movement, contact launch, landing, and terminal goal apply.
interaction_equivalence.physics_timing_tolerances_success: Shared narrow support checks, 840 ms flight, landing requirement, and radius 0.62 terminal tolerance.
interaction_equivalence.input_surface_binding: Full and simplified event sources are distinct and the grader rejects stale or wrong-mode transcripts.

evidence.explanation: The same state and canvas render while interaction chooses the control surface.
The grader requires the exact interaction condition and source mapping.

interaction_equivalence.world_and_information: Both modes receive the same four-launcher d5 chamber and terminal geometry; simplified labels expose the gallery as proxies.
interaction_equivalence.goal_and_effects: Three-stage construction, stair, launcher, movement, contact flight, landing, and terminal effects are unchanged.
interaction_equivalence.physics_timing_tolerances_success: Shared launch physics, route failures, and radius 0.55 terminal tolerance.

evidence.explanation: The oracle covers all ten level/mode variants.
Final success is based on shared physical state and exact configuration.

findings.claim: The source does not establish a uniquely screenshot-readable cue for the required stair end before commitment.
findings.causal_explanation: The generator derives the required side from the chamber mirror and the browser copies it into local requiredStairEnd state. Before selection, the renderer gives both sides the same provisional height and displays only CLICK ONE END · 3 / 2 / 1; the grader requires the hidden required_stair_end. Mirror-dependent block placement may be intended as a cue, but the source alone does not prove reliable screenshot inference.

evidence.explanation: The answer is derived from a seeded mirror.
Final left/right step heights depend on that answer.
Before selection the stair uses a symmetric provisional height and generic instruction.
The browser reads the mirror into local route state and simplified controls directly label both answers.
The grader requires the exact hidden stair answer.

findings.recommended_action: Perform the separate screenshot/human cue check. If the route cue is not reliably visible before commitment, render an explicit geometric cue or provide safe recovery.

findings.claim: The d4-to-d5 step is structurally real but weakly separated as a new difficulty level.
findings.causal_explanation: D5 keeps the red target at three and uses the same launch/route mechanism. It adds one actionable launcher and tighter width, stair rise, landing route, and terminal radius, but its other increases are longer traversal, lower movement speed, and one noninteractive decoy. These do not create a new state-changing planning dependency.

evidence.explanation: D4 and d5 retain red_stage_target 3 while changing gallery size and geometry.
Decoys are rendered as question-mark blocks.
Decoy hit targets are decoration and have no action handler.

findings.recommended_action: Calibrate d4 and d5 across seeds. Add a meaningful changing-state dependency or recovery burden to d5, or keep it as a harder d4 variant.

findings.claim: The d2-to-d3 physical difficulty ordering can vary by seed.
findings.causal_explanation: D2 forces its required launcher to be wall-facing, creating lateral contact and landing. D3 adds a second choice and tighter geometry, but its required launcher is floor-facing for an even required index and wall-facing for an odd index. D3 has greater decision load but can have an easier physical launcher on some seeds.

evidence.explanation: The generator forces d2 wall orientation and permits d3 floor/wall variation.
D3 adds launcher count and tighter geometry without uniform orientation increase.

findings.recommended_action: Measure success and completion time across seeds, or normalize required launcher orientation if monotone ordering is required.

findings.claim: decoy_actuator_count changes visible clutter but not the action or success problem.
findings.causal_explanation: The generator adds decoy actuators and the renderer draws them, but hit testing classifies them as decoration and the click handler has no branch that activates them. They may impose perceptual search cost, but add no actionable choice or state dependency.

evidence.explanation: Decoys are generated as separate red/yellow-decoy actuators.
Decoys are drawn as question-mark blocks.
Decoy hit tests are decoration; only red, yellow, launcher, and terminal hits cause actions.

findings.recommended_action: Treat decoys as visual search clutter only; do not count them as extra actuator decisions without separate perceptual calibration.

concise_summary: Rising Causeway d4/full is provisionally a plausible L4 first-person 3D planning-and-control task and its two interaction modes preserve the generated world, physics, goal, and grader contract. The ladder has a meaningful d1-to-d4 progression, but d4-to-d5 is weakly separated because red staging does not increase and decoys/longer traversal are not new state dependencies. The stair-side cue needs a separate screenshot/human check because the source renders a symmetric pre-selection stair while grading a mirror-derived answer.
limitations: No browser, runtime, human, or computer-use-agent checks were performed.
No previous audit, historical pre-controls implementation, or external review was used.
Absolute level placement remains provisional without cross-seed calibration.
